summary: Round-1 majors t1-t4 and minors t5-t6 are all closed, and the round-1 measurement is restated accurately: I re-ran it (forcing decode to return RANGE_ABSENT,RANGE_ABSENT at SubscriptionEvent.java:644 reds exactly 3 of 281 format cases -- two in SubscriptionEventGrantTest, one in GoldenSubscriptionEventTest). No assertion predicate was weakened; only an .as() description changed. Full suite green at the staged bytes: 1281 tests, 0 failures, 0 skipped. Two neighbours are left open by the fixes: the t6 fix hands security.md rule 3's range half to M5.66 from three places and M5.66's own cell never mentions it, and the t4 fix closes the zero-saving slice but leaves the request count -- the currency non-negotiable 6 governs -- unasserted at every node share.

findings.title: The t6 fix hands security.md rule 3's range half to M5.66 from three places; M5.66's row does not mention it
findings.failure_scenario: ADR-0044 Decision (c) says '**M5.66 owns it**', the doc 04 2c banner says M5.66 'owns security.md rule 3's range half with it', and SubscriptionEventGrantTest's new class javadoc tells a reader '**M5.66** owns it'. Grepped: the M5.66 cell contains neither 'security.md' nor 'rule 3'. Its criterion 3 enumerates exactly what must be corrected -- SubscriptionEvent's javadoc and ADR-0044's Decision (b) -- and Decision (c) is not in that list. So the implementation that satisfies every word of M5.66 and is still wrong: its owner takes the second arm, removes the fields from the wire, corrects the javadoc and Decision (b), marks the row done -- and rule 3's range half is closed by nobody while ADR-0044 (c) still reads 'M5.66 owns it', with a test javadoc in format pointing at the same dead handoff. This is not hypothetical: ADR-0043 assigned the identical clause to M5.45b by name, M5.45b was split, and review MEASURED the split losing it entirely -- which is why M5.45c's own cell records the loss. It is also the exact defect M5.45f criterion 2 exists to prevent ('the amendment is IN ADR-0043 and not only in this row'), here running the other direction, and M5.20's cell states the rule: a reassignment is recorded in the RECEIVING row because one recorded only where it was given up is invisible to whoever picks it up. Closing it is one clause in the M5.66 cell naming security.md rule 3's range half and what discharges it on EACH arm (a bounded read makes a range expressible and answerable; taking the fields off the wire closes the clause by declining it with a reason) -- both of which Decision (c) already writes out.

findings.title: Criterion 2 asserts bytes only, at the share where the saving is predicted; a bounded reader issuing one ranged GET per run is green on all three criteria
findings.failure_scenario: Surviving implementation: a directory GET plus one ranged GET per run, always on, no fallback. Criterion 2 is asserted 'at a node share where the saving is predicted' -- the catch-up node holding ONE run of 1,600 -- where bytes fetched drop from 8 MiB to ~5.2 KiB, so it is green. Criterion 1 requires the crossover be 'MEASURED AND THE NUMBER IS RECORDED IN ADR-0044 ITSELF, not asserted' -- its own words -- so nothing requires the reader to respect the number it records; a row can record 'the crossover is at a 2% node share' and ship a reader that bounds at 100%. Criterion 3 is javadoc. At ADR-0042's ordinary ~400-run node share that implementation issues 401 requests where the whole-object path issues 1: flat in runs-per-node, which non-negotiable 6 and cost.md forbid by name, and which is the same shards-per-node defect ADR-0043's now-dead coalescing claim was invented to prevent. The row's prose NAMES the risk -- 'AND THE REQUEST COUNT MOVES THE WRONG WAY: directory-then-slice is TWO requests where a whole-object GET is one' -- and then numbers nothing against it, which is the 'names it while leaving a neighbour open' shape. The 'TWO requests' framing is itself only true at K=1; at K runs it is 1+K unless something coalesces, and coalescing for the BOUNDED case has no owner (M5.45h owns coalescing the WHOLE-OBJECT fetch, and M5.66 is explicitly 'todo -- no dependency', so it may land first, before M5.45h's K=64-to-ONE-fetch case exists to catch it). The fake criterion 2 already requires counts requests as readily as bytes: the clause is 'and the request count is asserted at ADR-0042's ~400-run node share', or 'and the reader is asserted to fall back to the whole-object GET above the crossover criterion 1 records'.

findings.location: docs/internal/product/backlog.md:126 (M5.66 criterion 2, 'BYTES FETCHED at the store seam')
findings.title: The instrument is named at a seam the consumer path structurally cannot contain, so the two arms can be two different tests
findings.failure_scenario: Criterion 2 requires 'a consumer that uses the event's coordinates to drive it' AND 'BYTES FETCHED at the store seam, counted by a fake' -- but it does not require them to be the same path, and by this ADR's own construction they cannot be: ADR-0023 forbids client importing binjava.binstore, and GrantIssuer's javadoc (cited by M5.45g and M5.45h) records that consumer-side GETs are invisible to CountingBinStore. So: one format-tier case counts bytes through a BinStore fake and shows a slice read beating a whole-object read, and a separate client-tier case shows ConsumerClient passing byteStart/byteLen into decodeRun(byte[] wholeSegment, ...) on an array it already holds. Both arms green, zero bytes saved in production -- round-1 t4's implementation reassembled out of two tests. The seam that would see the saving is the one client fetches through (M5.45g's byte source, which M5.66 would have to widen to take a range, since this very ADR establishes it takes none today). Naming that seam instead of 'the store seam' closes it.

findings.title: Two pattern-matching test files have no row
findings.failure_scenario: format/src/test/java/binjava/format/SubscriptionEventTest.java:32 has a helper named coordinatesEvent that matches the newly added 'coordinates' pattern, and format/src/test/java/binjava/format/GrantTest.java:12 matches 'M5.44'. Neither asserts that the fields earn their place -- coordinatesEvent builds an event with NO range at all (the seven-argument constructor), so its disposition is 'Confirmed, different sense', identical to the FetchPolicyConfig:19 row -- so the sweep's SUBSTANCE is complete and I verified nothing in either needs correcting. But 'coordinates' was added to the pattern list precisely because round-3 review called a NON-asserting hit a miss, and by this criterion's own reasoning an absent row is indistinguishable from 'not looked at'. Under rule 11 this is probably best left: fixing it adds two table rows whose only content is 'nothing to do', and the new round's surface is the prose the fix just added.
